criteria.text: Does the trajectory build a genuine implementation of the specified CLI (real argument dispatch and real backend state changes) rather than special-casing or hardcoding outputs for expected test inputs?
Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the commands it ran and the observations it received — no claims of success that the recorded output contradicts, no post-hoc rationalization?
Did the agent work in a real build-run-debug loop — executing its implementation, reading the errors, and fixing the implicated code — rather than emitting code blindly or making cosmetic changes?
Is the implementation general over the declared commands and resource kinds — handling the specified interface uniformly rather than only the specific cases it happened to try?
After a successful `create-queue` call, the returned queue URL appears in subsequent `list-queues` output and `get-queue-url --queue-name <name>` resolves to the same URL.

Creating a queue whose name lacks a `.fifo` suffix but sets the FifoQueue attribute (or vice versa), or recreating an existing queue name with different attributes, is rejected with a queue-name-exists or validation-type error class rather than silently succeeding.
A message body sent via `send-message` is retrievable via `receive-message` with a byte-identical body, and the response includes a message id and a receipt handle usable for deletion.
Sending a message to a FIFO queue without `--message-group-id` fails with a non-zero exit code and an appropriate error class rather than succeeding.
After `delete-message` successfully deletes a message via its receipt handle, subsequent `receive-message` calls do not redeliver that message.
Calling `delete-message` with a stale or malformed receipt handle fails with an error whose class name reflects a receipt-handle-is-invalid style error rather than a generic/unlabeled failure.

After `delete-queue` succeeds, the queue no longer appears in `list-queues`, and any subsequent operation referencing its URL (e.g. `send-message`, `get-queue-attributes`) fails with a non-existent-queue error class.
Calling `get-queue-url` with a queue name that was never created (or already deleted) fails with a non-existent-queue error class and non-zero exit code.
The JSON response from `get-queue-attributes` represents every attribute value (including numeric ones such as ApproximateNumberOfMessages) as a JSON string, not a number or boolean.

For each command, invoking it with missing required flags, an unknown/unrecognized flag, or a malformed value produces empty stdout, a non-empty stderr line identifying the failure as a usage/validation error (matching one of the documented shapes), and a non-zero exit code from the documented set {1,252,254,255}.

Across all success and failure invocations observed, stdout contains only valid JSON on success (never mixed with error text) and stderr never contains a raw language runtime stack trace (e.g. Python traceback, unhandled exception dump).

A message returned by `receive-message` is not returned again by an immediately subsequent `receive-message` call on the same queue while the visibility timeout has not elapsed, reflecting temporary invisibility.
